__meta.authoredBy: row-3 tranche-A agent, then row-3 tranche-B agent
__meta.covers: All 41 guides in scratch/row3/syntax-only.json, which is exactly the 41 test-runner.mjs reports as ⚪ [SYNTAX-ONLY]. Nothing else. The tranche-A keys are byte-identical to the committed file; this tranche only appended the 21 non-01-array-string keys and updated __meta.
__meta.entryShape: Entries mirror scripts/test-runner.mjs RUNTIME_TESTS so the splice is a straight assign: { cases: [{ name, args, expect }] } for pure functions — `expect` is the field test-runner.mjs actually reads, `name` is an extra label the runner drops and this file's mismatch table uses. { script: '…' } for the in-place/class APIs, which is the repo's existing convention for those (53 such entries already); scripts use assertEq(actual, expected, label) and end with console.log('ASSERT-OK n').
equivalenceNotes: 04-matrix/02-spiral-matrix.md is catalog `equivalence: exact`, `codec: json`, despite a matrix being the argument: the canonical returns a flat int[], so a `cases` entry with a nested-array arg is exactly right. Only the two in-place void canonicals in that module need `script` entries.

04-matrix/03-rotate-image.md, 04-matrix/04-set-matrix-zeroes.md and 04-matrix/05-game-of-life.md are `returnType: void` with `equivalence: ops-terminal-state-and-outputs`: the canonical mutates the matrix in place and returns undefined, so each case is a `script` entry asserting the terminal state of a fresh argument.

02-two-pointers/05-3sum.md and 03-sliding-window/03-substring-with-concatenation-of-all-words.md are `equivalence: order-insensitive`, so their `script` entries sort the result before asserting. 3Sum additionally sorts its own input array in place.
05-hashmap/05-group-anagrams.md is `equivalence: multiset`, so its `script` entry sorts both the groups and the words inside them.

05-hashmap/03-word-pattern.md is `equivalence: exact`, NOT order-insensitive — the canonical returns a boolean, so no ordering can differ. (Earlier row-3 notes called it order-sensitive; the committed catalog does not.)

06-intervals/01-summary-ranges.md returns an array of STRINGS. Its `expect` values are string literals, and test-runner.mjs compares JSON.stringify on both sides, so the comparison is string-to-string.

02-two-pointers/02-is-subsequence.md has `fnName.L3 = null` because its Level 3 block declares a class (SubsequenceMatcher), not a bare function. test-cases.mjs needs a bare identifier to interpolate, so this guide is a `script` entry.

06-intervals/03-insert-interval.md and 06-intervals/04-minimum-number-of-arrows-to-burst-balloons.md have canonicals that MUTATE their first argument (newInterval is absorbed in place; points is sorted in place). Every case re-parses its args from JSON, so no case can leak state into the next.
__meta.keyRules: Keys are guide PATHS relative to the repo root, never slugs (plan E30). Keys starting with "__" are metadata, not guides — filter them before splicing into RUNTIME_TESTS. Key order is sorted, so the 20 tranche-A keys keep their committed positions and the 21 tranche-B keys sort after them. To splice: drop __meta, assign the rest into RUNTIME_TESTS, and re-serialize.
__meta.nonDeterminism: No tranche-B canonical is non-deterministic: none of the 21 Level 3 blocks reads Math.random, Date or any external state (plan edge case E26 wants a fixed input for those). 05-hashmap/08-contains-duplicate-ii.md does mention Date.now(), but only inside Follow-Up 2 (class SlidingWindowRateLimiter), never in the Level 3 canonical that these cases execute. Tranche A already covers the one random guide in the 41 — 01-array-string/12-insert-delete-getrandom-o1.md — by stubbing Math.random with a fixed draw sequence.
__meta.outstanding: None. The kill criterion (more than 15 of the 41 guides genuinely wrong) was not reached — see the MISMATCH table printed by node scripts/test-cases.mjs.
__meta.partial: COMPLETE. All 41 guides listed in scratch/row3/syntax-only.json have authored cases: 20 from tranche A (01-array-string/) and 21 from tranche B (02-two-pointers, 03-sliding-window, 04-matrix, 05-hashmap, 06-intervals, 07-stack). Nothing is outstanding.
